answer: One defense prices every new agent identity in verifiable useful work: before a clone can vote or earn, it must complete graded tasks that peers audit and sign, like climbing a cedar ridge of ever harder problems. A sybil fleet gets no velvet shortcut; each fake identity must independently redo that compute, so ten thousand clones cost ten thousand times the GPU-hours. The attacker pays real energy per head, which collapses the economics of mass impersonation.
